```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("DeCarlo_2026_carboplatin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("DeCarlo_2026_carboplatin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70413>
* PK layer: <https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-05-1076> (Ekhart 2006)

De Carlo et al. built a population PK-PD model of carboplatin-induced
thrombocytopenia and neutropenia from routine electronic-health-record data,
for model-informed precision dosing. No carboplatin concentrations were
available, so the PK is the Ekhart 2006 two-compartment model held fixed and
individualised only through its covariates (age, weight, sex and serum
creatinine). Two Friberg semi-mechanistic myelosuppression models, one for
platelets (PLT) and one for neutrophils (NT, here `ANC`), are driven by the
plasma carboplatin concentration through a linear inhibition of the
proliferation rate.

# Population

The model was developed on 580 adult cancer patients treated with carboplatin
at Amsterdam UMC between January 2019 and June 2022 (De Carlo 2026 Table 1):
median age 68 years (95% range 39-84), median weight 73 kg (50-116), 49%
female, median CKD-EPI eGFR 85.89 (37.80-115.91), median serum creatinine
72 umol/L (45-139) and median serum albumin 37 g/L (25-47). Diagnoses were
lung cancer (52%), gynaecological cancer (16%) and oesophageal/gastric cancer
(32%); 51% received concomitant paclitaxel and 70% concomitant pemetrexed. The
training data held 3635 platelet and 2726 neutrophil counts. A further 210
patients treated between June 2022 and January 2024 (Table S1.1) were used to
evaluate Bayesian next-cycle forecasts.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("DeCarlo_2026_carboplatin")()$population`.

# Steady state without drug

With no carboplatin the feedback term is 1 and both chains must stay at their
covariate-adjusted baselines. This is a structural check of the ODEs and the
initial conditions.

```{r steady-state}
mod <- readModelDb("DeCarlo_2026_carboplatin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

cov_typ <- data.frame(
  AGE = 68, WT = 73, SEXF = 0, CREAT = 72, ALB = 44, CRCL = 100,
  CONMED_PACLITAXEL = 0, CONMED_PEMETREXED = 0, TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC = 0,
  CYCLE = 1
)

# Observation rows name an ODE state; dvid = 1 returns every endpoint column.
obs_ss <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 10, 50, 100), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
  cmt = "circ_plt", dvid = 1L
)
ss <- rxSolve(mod_typ, cbind(obs_ss, cov_typ), returnType = "data.frame")
ss[, c("time", "PLT", "ANC")]
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss$PLT - 293) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(ss$ANC - 5.16) < 1e-6)
)
```

# Carboplatin PK: clearance and exposure

The PK is fixed, so a subject's clearance is a deterministic function of age,
weight, sex and serum creatinine (Ekhart 2006 model 4). For a 68-year-old,
73 kg man with creatinine 72 umol/L the clearance is
115.5 + 0.212 x 72 x 73 / 72 = 131.0 mL/min, close to the 138.8 mL/min
(8.33 L/h) Ekhart 2006 reported as the mean population clearance.

The PK is checked with PKNCA on a single 30-minute infusion dosed by the
Calvert formula (AUC 5 mg.min/mL, using the Cockcroft-Gault estimate of GFR)
in a virtual cohort drawn from the Table 1 ranges. The NCA AUC must equal
dose / CL for every subject, because the PK has no random effects.

```{r pk-cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_pk <- 100
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_pk),
  AGE = round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pk, 66, 11), 39), 84)),
  WT = round(pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_pk, log(73), 0.2), 50), 116)),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_pk, 1, 0.49),
  CREAT = round(pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_pk, log(72), 0.3), 45), 139))
) |>
  mutate(
    crcl_cg = (140 - AGE) * WT * ifelse(SEXF == 1, 0.85, 1) / (0.815 * CREAT),
    dose = 5 * (crcl_cg + 25),
    cl_mlmin = 115.5 + 0.212 * (140 - AGE) * WT * 0.736^SEXF / CREAT,
    ALB = 37, CRCL = 86, CONMED_PACLITAXEL = 0, CONMED_PEMETREXED = 1,
    TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC = 0, CYCLE = 1, treatment = "AUC5 single dose"
  )

t_obs <- c(0, seq(0.25, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 96, by = 1)) / 24
ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = dose, rate = dose / (0.5 / 24),
                      evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = t_obs) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, AGE, WT, SEXF, CREAT, ALB, CRCL,
                              CONMED_PACLITAXEL, CONMED_PEMETREXED,
                              TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC, CYCLE, treatment),
            by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# The PK has no random effects, so the typical-value model gives every
# subject's exact concentrations; rxode2's notice about a multi-subject solve
# without omega is expected here and is the only warning muffled.
sim_pk <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "treatment"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
)
```

```{r pk-nca}
conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
doses <- cohort |> transmute(id, time = 0, dose, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(doses, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
                        half.life = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

auc <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, dose, cl_mlmin), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    # mg.day/L to mg.min/mL: x 1440 min/day / 1000 mL/L
    auc_mgminml = aucinf * 1.44,
    auc_closed = dose / cl_mlmin,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc_mgminml - auc_closed) / auc_closed
  )
summary(nca)
```

The NCA AUC and the closed form `dose / CL` use the same individual clearance,
so they differ only by trapezoidal and extrapolation error:

```{r pk-check}
summary(auc$pct_diff)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc$pct_diff) < 2))
```

The Calvert formula targets an AUC of 5 mg.min/mL; with the Ekhart clearance
the achieved AUC differs, which is the mismatch the paper's discussion
attributes to creatinine-based GFR estimates. The median achieved AUC in this
cohort:

```{r pk-calvert}
summary(auc$auc_mgminml)
```

# Replicating Figure 5: covariate effects on platelets and neutrophils

Figure 5 simulates a typical oesophageal/gastric cancer patient on weekly
carboplatin (Calvert AUC 2, five doses on days 0-28) with paclitaxel and
radiotherapy, varying one covariate at a time: serum albumin (25, 44 and
47 g/L; panels A-B), CKD-EPI eGFR (38, 100 and 116; panel C) and paclitaxel
co-medication (panel D). The paper does not give the patient's age, weight,
sex, creatinine or the GFR used in the Calvert formula; the Table 1 medians
(68 years, 73 kg, male, creatinine 72 umol/L) and a Calvert GFR of 100 mL/min
(dose 250 mg) are assumed here. Each weekly dose is counted as one treatment
cycle. Lines are medians and ribbons 90% intervals of 100 simulated patients
per scenario.

```{r fig5-sim}
n_per <- 100
scen <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(panel = "A-B", level = c("ALB 25 g/L", "ALB 44 g/L", "ALB 47 g/L"),
             ALB = c(25, 44, 47), CRCL = 100, CONMED_PACLITAXEL = 1),
  data.frame(panel = "C", level = c("eGFR 38", "eGFR 100", "eGFR 116"),
             ALB = 44, CRCL = c(38, 100, 116), CONMED_PACLITAXEL = 1),
  data.frame(panel = "D", level = c("PTX no", "PTX yes"),
             ALB = 44, CRCL = 100, CONMED_PACLITAXEL = c(0, 1))
) |>
  mutate(scenario = seq_len(n()))

subj <- tidyr::expand_grid(scenario = scen$scenario, rep = seq_len(n_per)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n())) |>
  left_join(scen, by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(AGE = 68, WT = 73, SEXF = 0, CREAT = 72, CONMED_PEMETREXED = 0,
         TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC = 1)

dose_wk <- 2 * (100 + 25)
t_grid <- seq(0, 35, by = 0.5)
ev5 <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = c(0, 7, 14, 21, 28)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_wk, rate = dose_wk / (0.5 / 24), evid = 1L,
           cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = t_grid) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "circ_plt", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(CYCLE = pmin(floor(time / 7), 4) + 1) |>
  left_join(subj |> select(id, panel, level, AGE, WT, SEXF, CREAT, ALB, CRCL,
                            CONMED_PACLITAXEL, CONMED_PEMETREXED,
                            TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC),
            by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# Tight tolerances: in subjects with a large drug-effect slope the
# proliferating pool falls many orders of magnitude, and the default
# tolerances can step it below zero, where (circ0 / circ)^gamma is NaN.
sim5 <- rxSolve(mod, ev5, returnType = "data.frame",
                keep = c("panel", "level"),
                atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  filter(time %in% t_grid)

# A subject drawn far in the tail of the slope distribution can drive its
# proliferating pool so close to zero that the solver steps it negative and
# the trajectory diverges. Such subjects are dropped and counted.
diverged <- unique(sim5$id[!is.finite(sim5$PLT) | !is.finite(sim5$ANC)])
cat("Subjects with a diverged solve:", length(diverged), "of", nrow(subj), "\n")
stopifnot(length(diverged) / nrow(subj) < 0.02)
sim5 <- sim5 |> filter(!(id %in% diverged))

sum5 <- sim5 |>
  pivot_longer(c(PLT, ANC), names_to = "output", values_to = "count") |>
  group_by(panel, level, output, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(count), lo = quantile(count, 0.05),
            hi = quantile(count, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 8}
fig5 <- bind_rows(
  sum5 |> filter(panel == "A-B", output == "PLT") |> mutate(p = "A: PLT by albumin"),
  sum5 |> filter(panel == "A-B", output == "ANC") |> mutate(p = "B: NT by albumin"),
  sum5 |> filter(panel == "C", output == "ANC") |> mutate(p = "C: NT by CKD-EPI eGFR"),
  sum5 |> filter(panel == "D", output == "PLT") |> mutate(p = "D: PLT by paclitaxel")
)
ggplot(fig5, aes(time, med, colour = level, fill = level)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 7, 14, 21, 28), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~p, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Count (10^9/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of De Carlo 2026") +
  theme_bw()
```

Day-35 medians from the simulation, next to values read from the published
Figure 5:

```{r fig5-table}
fig5_pub <- data.frame(
  p = c("A: PLT by albumin", "B: NT by albumin", "C: NT by CKD-EPI eGFR",
        "D: PLT by paclitaxel", "D: PLT by paclitaxel"),
  level = c("ALB 44 g/L", "ALB 44 g/L", "eGFR 100", "PTX no", "PTX yes"),
  published_day0 = c(260, 4.75, 4.75, 260, 260),
  published_day35 = c(110, 2.5, 2.4, 110, 170)
)
fig5 |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 35)) |>
  select(p, level, time, med) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = med, names_prefix = "sim_day") |>
  inner_join(fig5_pub, by = c("p", "level")) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Panel" = p, "Scenario" = level,
    "Simulated day 0" = sim_day0, "Simulated day 35" = sim_day35,
    "Figure 5 day 0" = published_day0, "Figure 5 day 35" = published_day35
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The baselines and the direction and ordering of every covariate effect match
Figure 5: low albumin raises both baselines and deepens the platelet decline,
low eGFR deepens the neutrophil decline while 100 and 116 nearly overlap, and
paclitaxel blunts the platelet decline.

The platelet curve of panel A (paclitaxel-treated patient, albumin 44 g/L)
is reproduced closely, about 106 against about 110 x 10^9/L at day 35.
Two differences remain, and the model was not tuned to close either:

* The neutrophil panels B and C fall further than published (about 1.5
  against about 2.5 x 10^9/L at day 35), although neutrophils carry no
  cycle effect. Since the platelet curve agrees at the same exposure, an
  exposure difference alone does not explain it; the unstated PK covariates
  of the published patient remain one possible source. A typical-value
  dose of about 150 mg instead of 250 mg would reproduce the published
  neutrophil curve.
* Panel D is not consistent with panel A in the paper itself. The caption
  places the panel A patient on paclitaxel, and panel A ends near 110,
  but panel D's paclitaxel curve ends near 170 and its no-paclitaxel curve
  near 110. The simulation gives about 114 (paclitaxel) and 53 (no
  paclitaxel), which agrees with panel A rather than with panel D.

```{r fig5-check}
d35 <- fig5 |> filter(time == 35)
alb <- d35 |> filter(p == "A: PLT by albumin")
stopifnot(
  # Albumin: lower albumin, higher platelet count throughout.
  alb$med[alb$level == "ALB 25 g/L"] > alb$med[alb$level == "ALB 47 g/L"],
  # Paclitaxel blunts the platelet decline.
  with(d35 |> filter(p == "D: PLT by paclitaxel"),
       med[level == "PTX yes"] > med[level == "PTX no"]),
  # Reduced renal function deepens the neutrophil decline.
  with(d35 |> filter(p == "C: NT by CKD-EPI eGFR"),
       med[level == "eGFR 38"] < med[level == "eGFR 100"])
)
```

# Cumulative platelet toxicity over cycles

The platelet drug-effect slope rises linearly with the cycle number
(`1 + 0.756 * CYCLE`), so the same dose produces deeper platelet nadirs in
later cycles; neutrophils carry no such effect. A typical lung cancer patient
(pemetrexed, no paclitaxel, albumin 37 g/L, eGFR 86) on four cycles of
Calvert AUC 5 every 3 weeks:

```{r cycles}
dose_q3w <- 5 * (86 + 25)
t_c <- seq(0, 84, by = 0.5)
ev_c <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 21, 42, 63), amt = dose_q3w,
             rate = dose_q3w / (0.5 / 24), evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
             dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = t_c, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L,
             cmt = "circ_plt", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(CYCLE = pmin(floor(time / 21), 3) + 1, AGE = 68, WT = 73, SEXF = 0,
         CREAT = 72, ALB = 37, CRCL = 86, CONMED_PACLITAXEL = 0,
         CONMED_PEMETREXED = 1, TUMTP_ESOPHAGOGASTRIC = 0) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
sim_c <- rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_c, returnType = "data.frame",
                 atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  filter(time %in% t_c) |>
  mutate(cycle = pmin(floor(time / 21), 3) + 1)

nadir <- sim_c |>
  group_by(cycle) |>
  summarise(PLT_nadir = min(PLT), ANC_nadir = min(ANC), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(nadir, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(diff(nadir$PLT_nadir) < 0))
```

```{r cycles-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_c |>
  select(time, PLT, ANC) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 21, 42, 63), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Count (10^9/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK layer.** The paper fixes the PK to Ekhart 2006 but prints only the
  clearance equation (Eq. S1.1). The central volume (16.3 L) and the
  micro-constants k12 (0.104 1/h) and k21 (0.171 1/h) are taken from
  Ekhart 2006 Table 2, which reports them for the covariate-free reference
  model; Ekhart 2006 does not tabulate separate values for the creatinine
  model whose clearance equation De Carlo used. All PK parameters are fixed
  and carry no random effects, as in the source.
* **Unit conversions.** The clearance equation returns mL/min (x 1.44 to
  L/day) and the Ekhart micro-constants are per hour (x 24 to 1/day); the
  model runs in days to match the maturation times. Concentrations are in
  mg/L, matching the L/mg units of the drug-effect slopes.
* **Treatment cycle counter.** Eq. S2.1 writes
  `SlopePLT * (1 + beta * Treat.Cycle)` without defining the origin of
  `Treat.Cycle`. The model uses the 1-based cycle number (`CYCLE = 1` in the
  first cycle), so the tabulated 0.282 L/mg is the value extrapolated to
  `CYCLE = 0` and the first-cycle typical slope is 0.282 x 1.756. A 0-based
  counter would make every cycle's slope 1.756-fold smaller. In the Figure 5
  replication the 1-based counter reproduces the panel A platelet curve
  (day 35 about 106 against about 110 x 10^9/L published), while a 0-based
  counter gives about 135 for the typical patient. For
  weekly regimens each weekly dose is counted as a cycle here; the paper does
  not say how it numbered weekly administrations.
* **Pemetrexed, not paclitaxel, on the neutrophil baseline.** Eq. S2.1 prints
  `beta_PTX * PTX` in the Circ0NT line, but Table 2, Table S2.1, the Step 3
  covariate list and the correlation-matrix label `beta_Circ0_NT_pem_TRUE`
  all name pemetrexed, and the coefficient (0.355) is the Table 2 pemetrexed
  value. The model uses pemetrexed.
* **IIV labels.** Table 2 labels its second block of four omegas "PLT"
  (and repeats "gammaPLT"). They are read as the neutrophil omegas in the
  order Circ0, MTT, gamma, Slope, mirroring the platelet block and the eight
  random effects of Eq. S2.1. Table 2 reports omegas and sigmas as SDs.
* **Residual error.** The platelet error combines additive and proportional
  terms; the paper does not say which Monolix form. The Monolix default
  `combined1` (`a + b * f`, SDs added) is used.
* **eGFR units.** The paper labels CKD-EPI eGFR as mL/min; the covariate is
  supplied as the CKD-EPI equation computes it (mL/min/1.73 m^2). The main
  text cites the 2009 equation and the Table S1.1 footnote the 2021 one.
* **Time-varying covariates.** Albumin, eGFR, weight and creatinine were
  time-varying in the source. The model reads them row by row, so a change in
  albumin also moves the circulating baselines that the feedback term targets.
* **Solver tolerances.** With the linear drug effect, `1 - Slope * Conc` is
  strongly negative around each infusion, so in subjects with a large
  slope the proliferating pool falls by many orders of magnitude before it
  recovers. Default tolerances can then step it below zero and return `NaN`
  from the feedback term. The simulations here use `atol = 1e-12` and
  `rtol = 1e-10`, and the rare simulated subject whose solve still diverges
  (a draw far in the tail of the slope distribution) is dropped from the
  Figure 5 summaries and counted in the output.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (LDH, capecitabine, etoposide,
  radiotherapy, immunotherapy, age, sex, weight and Cockcroft-Gault GFR on
  the PD) are not in the model; the first four are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
